title: Integration & Release Orchestration Playbook for Inference Runtime
author: Aisha Park
content:
Summary
This playbook defines the cross-cutting requirements and step-by-step orchestration for integrated releases of the Redwood inference runtime. It bridges runtime architecture decisions, kernel scheduling rollouts, profiling/benchmark gates, runbook rehearsals, and the final release note artifact. Use this document for minor to major releases (feature flags, kernel variants, scheduler changes, quantization profile updates).

Goals
- Reduce production regressions by standardizing preflight and canary criteria.
- Ensure observability and cost telemetry are sufficient to diagnose degradation within 10 minutes.
- Provide a repeatable, auditable sequence for rollouts with clear owners and rollback criteria.

Scope and applicability
Applies to: serving runtime service (runtime-coordinator), kernel dispatcher (kernel-dispatcher), KV cache controller (kvcache-controller), scheduler API (schedulerd), and integration components (orchestrator-api, perf-runner). Notably this playbook includes: kernel scheduling policy changes, kernel binary rollouts, runtime feature flags (continuous batching, predictive-prefetch), and changes to telemetry retention that affect profiling.

Who should read this
- Release engineers coordinating the deploy (owner: runtime-release).
- Kernel and scheduler owners (team: kernel-scheduling).
- Profiling and benchmarking leads (team: perf-eng).
- Oncall SREs and maintainer of the canary and chaos tooling.

High-level release flow (summary)
1) Design and risk assessment (RFC + ADR entry)
2) Local developer verification (unit tests + e2e in sandbox)
3) Controlled bench runs (perf-runner + shadow replay)
4) Canary release (progressive percentages) with automated gates
5) Ramp and monitoring window (24–72 hours depending on risk)
6) Full release and release note publish

Preflight checklist (must pass all items)
| Check | Command / Location | Acceptable value | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| ADR linked | confluence RFC link | RFC+ADR present | feature-owner |
| Unit + integration tests | CI: runtime-ci/pipeline | green | eng-ci |
| Kernel binary signature | sigstore verify kernel-v*.sig | verified | kernel-scheduling |
| Perf warm-run | perf-runner --profile=warm --runs=100 | p95 < 120ms | perf-eng |
| Synthetic tail test | perf-runner --profile=tail --duration=30m | p99 < 350ms | perf-eng |
| Memory regression check | kvbench --alloc-check | no >10% reg | runtime-release |
| Telemetry schema validation | telemetry-lint schema/runtime-telemetry.yaml | ok | observability |
| Runbook rehearsal | playbook-runner simulate --incident=latency-spike | success | eng-sre |

Design and risk assessment
- For any kernel/scheduler change the author must produce a concise risk assessment with: affected models, sequence length distribution shift, expected kernel path changes, and potential memory/regression vectors.
- Attach the following artifacts to the RFC: microbenchmark results (csv), kernel trace samples (gzip), and a short rollout plan.

Local verification (developer sandbox)
- Use the runtime sandbox image: registry.redwood.internal/runtime-sandbox:dev-<sha>.
- Commands to run basic verification:
  1. Start local runtime: docker compose -f runtime-sandbox/docker-compose.yml up --build
  2. Run unit e2e: ./scripts/e2e_local.sh --model=llama-mini --seq=256 --concurrency=4
  3. Collect trace: curl -H 'X-Debug-Trace: on' http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}' > trace.json

Profiling and benchmark gating
- All releases must run the following benchmark set on the approved infra matrix (see infra-accounts-and-networking docs):
  a) Microbench kernel suite (kernel-harness): 10k iterations across seq=[8,64,256,1024]
  b) Mixed workload replay (perf-runner shadow mode) with production-weighted request surface for 60 minutes
  c) Cost sensitivity sweep: measure per-token energy and unit cost at concurrency points [1,8,32]
- Success criteria: no regressions > 5% in p95 or cost-per-token vs baseline; no memory OOM regressions; no new kernel assertion logs.
- Example perf-runner command: perf-runner --matrix infra:dgx-pool --scenario=shadow-replay --duration=60m --baseline=S2026-09-01 --output=results/rel-<tag>.json

Automated gates and canary policy
- Canary progression policy (automated): 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with hold times: 15m, 30m, 2h, 6h respectively.
- Gate checks executed at each hold:
  - Latency SLA: p95 < 120ms and p99 < 350ms (applicable for conversational models).
  - Error budget: error-rate increase <= 0.05 absolute or 50% relative (whichever more conservative).
  - Kernel health: no more than 0.1% kernel restarts and no assertion logs sampled in last 5 minutes.
  - Cost signal: unit-cost delta <= +15% in the canary pool vs baseline.
- Gate automation: orchestrator-api triggers canary progress; the gate runner posts status to #release-ops and creates a canary check artifact in S3: s3://release-artifacts/canary/<tag>/checks.json

Rollback and abort criteria (explicit)
- Immediate rollback triggers (abort and roll back to previous release):
  - p99 latency increases > 100ms sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Error-rate absolute increase > 0.2% sustained for 5 minutes.
  - Any kernel crash loop or nvml thermal emergency event.
- Soft abort where manual operator review is required: memory increase > 15% but below OOM, cost jump > 25% with no latency regression.
- Rollback procedure (fast path):
  1. orchestrator-api rollback --to-tag <previous-tag>
  2. kube rollout status deployment/runtime-coordinator -n runtime --watch
  3. Purge canary traffic: routerctl set-weight runtime-canary 0
  4. Dispatch incident: incident create --severity=sev2 --title "Rollback: runtime <tag> -> <previous-tag>" --owners runtime-release,eng-sre

Runbooks and incident rehearsals
- Required runbook templates included at the end of this doc must be rehearsed quarterly for each team: kernel-scheduling, runtime-release, perf-eng, eng-sre.
- Example runbook snippet (latency spike):
  - Signal: p99 >= threshold for 10 minutes, p95 rising faster than baseline
  - Triage steps:
    1. Identify cohort: query trace-index for request cohorts with X-Trace-Tag
    2. Check kernel dispatch queues: curl -s http://kernel-dispatcher.internal/queues | jq .queue_depths
    3. Validate KV cache hit-rate: redis-cli -h kvcache-prod info | grep hits
    4. If kernel queue depth > 80% and backlog growing -> reduce batch-window by setting: curl -X POST http://schedulerd.internal/config -d '{"batch_window_ms":50}'

Telemetry and retention requirements
- Minimum telemetry retained for release vetting: 90 days of request-level aggregates, 30 days of full trace blobs, 365 days of change metadata and kernel-version mapping.
- Example retention config (YAML):
  telemetry_retention:
    aggregates_days: 90
    traces_days: 30
    metadata_days: 365

- Cost-slicing telemetry: ensure cost signals are emitted per-token and per-request: fields in runtime-telemetry.jsonl must include: [timestamp, model, sequence_length, tokens_generated, kernel_variant, cost_usd, gpu_seconds].

Known issues checklist to validate before release
- Confirm fix or acceptance for current known issues that can be triggered by kernel changes:
  - NVLINK degradation under heavy multi-GPU scatter (if affected, add network throttling to bench).
  - KVCache shard skew with quantized kernels (verify shard histograms).
  - GRPC connection reuse causing pipeline regeneration (verify connection reuse counters).
- Owners must attach issue IDs to the release artifact (Jira or internal tracker).

Post-release validations and release notes artifact
- After reaching 100%: run a 24-hour observation window where perf-runner generates a stability report. If stability OK, author final release notes including: what changed, affected services, rolling upgrade notes, rollback triggers observed, and list of validation artifacts (bench JSONs, kernel traces).
- Release notes template (to be copied into confluence release page):
  - Version: <tag>
  - Summary: short description of change
  - Risk: low/medium/high and rationale
  - Benchmarks: attach results links (S3) and highlight deltas vs baseline
  - Rollout timeline: canary timestamps and progression
  - Owners and oncall contacts
  - Known issues and mitigations

Operational tooling and commands (quick-reference)
- Canary orchestration: orchestrator-api canary --tag <tag> --policy progressive.json
- Kernel signature verification: sigstore verify --key k8s://sigstore-key kernel-v<ver>.sig
- Perf-run replay: perf-runner --scenario shadow-replay --input s3://shadow-corpora/<date>.tar.gz --duration 60m
- Collecting traces: /opt/runtime/bin/trace-exporter --from=2026-10-01T00:00Z --to=2026-10-01T01:00Z --out s3://trace-dump/<tag>.tgz

Governance and approvals
- Low-risk changes (e.g., telemetry retention config updates, observability schema) require: PR + perf-eng signoff.
- Medium-risk (kernel param changes, minor scheduler policy edits): PR + perf-eng + kernel-scheduling review + eng-sre rehearsal signoff.
- High-risk (new kernel binary, scheduling engine rewrite): Full RFC + cross-team design review meeting + blackbox bench pass + exec sponsor approval.

Appendices
A. Sample canary-checks.json template
{
  "tag": "<tag>",
  "checks": [
    {"name":"latency-p95","threshold_ms":120,"actual_ms":114},
    {"name":"error-rate","threshold_pct":0.05,"actual_pct":0.03}
  ]
}

B. Quick runbook for a kernel hotfix deployment
1) Patch kernel release branch and sign the artifact.
2) Upload to S3: aws s3 cp kernel-v<ver>.tgz s3://kernel-artifacts/<tag>/
3) Trigger canary with single-node pool: orchestrator-api canary --tag <tag> --pool kernel-hotfix-pool --policy single-step.json
4) Monitor kernel logs: kubectl logs -l app=kernel-dispatcher -n runtime --tail=200 | grep -i error
5) If any kernel assertion appears, abort: orchestrator-api rollback --to-tag <previous-tag>

C. Owner roster (primary contact for each phase)
- Design/RFC: Aisha Park (runtime-arch)
- Perf gating: Marta Li (perf-eng)
- Canary orchestration: Evan Thompson (runtime-release)
- Oncall contact: eng-sre pager duty rotation (see team wiki)

Document maintenance
- This playbook must be reviewed after any high-severity incident that involved releases, and on a cadence of 6 months. Update the canary progression timings and gate thresholds as the fleet and models evolve.
